title: Temporal control of sgRNA library activation unlocks large-scale in vivo CRISPR screens
model: A549 lung xenografts, CRISPR-StAR ~30,000-sgRNA inducible library; 118 + 49 tumors
contrast: Active vs inactive sgRNA (knockout effect), cohort-paired (118-mouse screen + 49-mouse validation)
paper_method: Per-clone Bayesian pipeline CSTAR-UMIBB (matched active/inactive within clone, clone-size weighted)
paper_calls: Essential-gene dropout (e.g. PLK1) reproducible with ~30 tumors; KMT2C and KMT2D opposite in vivo phenotypes; 173 in-vivo-specific hits
barcs_calls: 298 genes at FDR 0.10; essential vs non-essential AUC 0.90; 90/197 essentials depleted
named_hits: PLK1/MYC/KIF11 depleted (essential); KMT2D depleted and KMT2C enriched (opposite, as the paper reports); PTEN enriched (tumor suppressor)
verdict: Even using only bulk active/inactive aggregation (the proxy the paper shows is weaker than its per-clone method), BARCS separates essentials from controls at AUC 0.90, recovers PLK1, and reproduces the paper's headline that KMT2C and KMT2D have opposite in vivo phenotypes; it cannot reproduce the per-clone wtheta/Delta scores or the 173-gene in-vivo-specific list.
